memos.headline: JPM and MSFT Lead Relative Strength; UNH in Freefall, CAT and AMZN Lagging Hard
memos.body: I see a broad bounce this week across the universe—every name except UNH and PG posted positive 1-week returns—but the intermediate trend remains firmly down for most. JPM stands out as the only name trading above its 200-day mean (+4.5%) with the shallowest drawdown from highs (-13.0%) and positive 26-week return (+8.9%); it is the cleanest long setup here. MSFT has reclaimed its 50-day mean (+1.2%) and shows the best 4-week relative strength vs SPY (+3.2%), suggesting institutional rotation into quality mega-cap. UNH is a textbook breakdown: RSI 27.7, -33% from highs, -16.7% below its 50-day, and -23.6% below its 200-day—this is a falling knife I want no part of until it at least reclaims $450. CAT and AMZN show severe 12-week relative weakness vs SPY (-13.6% and -11.8% respectively) and remain well below both moving averages, making them avoid-to-neutral at best until structure improves.

views.note: Only name above 200d mean (+4.5%), shallowest drawdown (-13%), positive 26w return; would reassess on a close below $230.
Reclaimed 50d mean, best 4w rel strength vs SPY (+3.2%), RSI 56; invalidated below $370.
RSI 27.7, -33% from highs, massively below both moving averages—classic breakdown with no sign of stabilization; need a close above $450 to reconsider.

Defensive name weakening: -5.6% this week, RSI 42, but 12w rel strength vs SPY still positive (+5.4%); watch $157 support.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Show Strongest Earnings Power; PG and XOM Face Revenue Headwinds
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA (+77.9% YoY revenue, 56.2% net margin) and GOOGL (+11.8% revenue, 27.5% margin with only $14.79B debt), both demonstrating operating leverage and manageable balance sheets. MSFT continues to compound at +12.3% revenue growth with a 34.6% net margin and moderate $44.97B debt load, making it a reliable compounder. On the other side, PG posted a -2.1% YoY revenue decline in its March quarter with flat net income (+0.4%), and XOM saw revenue contract -1.1% with a thin 9.1% margin—both signal cash-flow compression risk. UNH's 5.5% net margin on $100.81B revenue with $76.90B in debt leaves very little room for error; any uptick in medical costs would change my view from neutral to avoid.

views.note: 77.9% YoY revenue growth and 56.2% net margin on only $8.46B debt is extraordinary earnings power; I'd reassess if margins compress below 40%.
11.8% revenue growth, 27.5% net margin, and a clean $14.79B debt load make this the best risk-adjusted earner in mega-cap tech.
12.3% revenue growth and 34.6% net margin with $44.97B debt is a durable compounder; would turn cautious if cloud segment growth decelerates below high single digits.
Net income nearly doubled YoY to $20B on 10.5% revenue growth, showing real margin expansion to 10.7%, but $58B debt warrants monitoring.
Only +4% revenue growth with $94.80B in total debt is the weakest top-line profile among mega-cap tech despite a solid 29.2% margin.
50.5% net income growth and 32.7% margin are impressive but likely peak-cycle; $401B debt is inherent to the model and credit losses could compress earnings quickly.
Only 5.5% net margin on $100.81B revenue with $76.90B debt leaves minimal buffer; any medical cost ratio deterioration would flip me to avoid.
Revenue declining -2.1% YoY with essentially flat net income (+0.4%) signals volume pressure that a 19.1% margin cannot offset indefinitely.
Revenue -1.1% and net income -0.3% with a 9.1% margin show commodity-driven earnings compression; would reconsider only on a sustained oil price recovery.
Revenue fell -5.0% YoY yet net income rose +4.4% showing cost discipline, but 17.2% margin sustainability depends on infrastructure spending holding up.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Cooling Inflation and Softening Labor Market — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the macro regime as a prolonged pause with an easing bias: the Fed has held the upper bound at 4.50% for three months while the 12-month change is -100 bp, CPI is running at just 2.4% y/y, and unemployment has drifted up 30 bp over the past year to 4.2%. The 10y yield at 4.29% has fallen 34 bp over three months and the 10y-2y spread has steepened 79 bp over 12 months to +0.55 pp, consistent with the market pricing eventual cuts and a mild growth slowdown. This backdrop favors duration-sensitive mega-cap growth names that benefit from lower discount rates and is less supportive of cyclicals and energy, which need accelerating nominal growth. A hot May CPI print above 0.4% m/m or a surprise rate hike would force me to revisit, as would unemployment breaking above 4.5%, which would shift the call from slowdown to outright recession risk.

views.note: High-quality duration asset that benefits from falling long-end yields and an easing-biased Fed pause.
Declining 10y yield and benign inflation support valuations for mega-cap growth with strong cash flows.
Duration-sensitive growth benefits from lower rates, though higher beta adds uncertainty in a slowdown.
Steepening curve (+79 bp y/y in 10y-2y) helps NIM, but rising unemployment and slowing growth cap upside.
Defensive staple holds up in a slowdown, but 2.4% CPI limits pricing power upside; fairly valued here.
Classic cyclical facing headwinds from rising unemployment and slowing nominal growth; not the right regime.
Energy needs accelerating nominal GDP; softening labor market and moderate CPI suggest demand-side risk.
Benefits from lower discount rates and consumer resilience while unemployment remains below 4.5%.
Ad-driven revenue may slow in a softening economy, but falling yields support the multiple; net positive.
Defensive healthcare name is regime-neutral; neither helped nor hurt materially by the current pause-to-ease setup.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: GOOGL and JPM Positive, UNH and PG Under Severe Pressure
memos.body: I see a clear split in sentiment trajectories across the universe this week. GOOGL reported Q1 results on 4/24 and the market rewarded it with a +1.7% move into the 4/25 close, suggesting the narrative is turning constructive after months of regulatory overhang. JPM's earnings on 4/11 drove a +4.0% one-day pop and subsequent filings show continued corporate activity, indicating positive momentum that may not yet be fully priced. On the negative side, UNH's 4/17 earnings triggered a devastating -22.4% single-day decline—the kind of sentiment shock that typically takes weeks to stabilize and often sees further downside as analysts revise. PG dropped -3.7% on its Q3 FY25 results filed 4/24, a meaningful miss for a defensive staple, and the accompanying earnings slides suggest the narrative around pricing power is weakening.

views.note: Positive earnings reaction of +1.7% signals a constructive narrative shift; tone is turning up from a cautious base.
Strong +4.0% post-earnings reaction and continued filing activity suggest positive sentiment momentum still has room to run.
A -22.4% single-day earnings collapse represents a severe sentiment regime change that historically takes extended time to repair.
The -3.7% earnings-day drop for a defensive staple signals deteriorating sentiment around the pricing-power narrative.
Recent filings are limited to board changes and an Other Events item with no earnings catalyst; sentiment signal is too thin to act on.
Multiple early-April filings cover routine corporate matters with no clear directional sentiment shift.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty and Export-Control Risk Weigh Heavily on Tech Supply Chains; Energy Weakness Signals Demand Concerns
memos.body: I see a geopolitical environment defined by structurally elevated policy uncertainty—the daily EPU index at 419.9 is up 122% over three months even after a modest one-month pullback, while VIX at 26.47 (+78% 3m) and HY OAS widening of +113bp 3m confirm markets are pricing sustained policy risk, not a one-off shock. WTI crude at $63.55 (down 15% 3m) suggests either demand destruction from trade-war friction or supply-side relief, but the combination with widening credit spreads points me toward the demand-destruction read. NVDA's mid-April 8-K (8.01 Other Events) lands in the window of tightening AI-chip export controls to China, which I treat as a structural headwind for its highest-margin data-center business. For domestically oriented names like JPM and PG, the risk is more cyclical than structural—tariff-driven inflation and slower growth—but their supply chains are less exposed to direct export-control or China-sourcing disruption. I would need a credible de-escalation in US-China tech restrictions or a meaningful tariff rollback to upgrade my stance on the most exposed names.

views.note: AI-chip export controls to China represent a structural margin and volume headwind that is unlikely to reverse near-term.
Heavy China manufacturing concentration exposes AAPL to tariff and supply-chain disruption risk in the current policy environment.
WTI at $63.55 and falling 15% 3m pressures upstream margins, but XOM's domestic asset base insulates it from direct trade-policy risk.
Steepening yield curve (+25bp 1m) supports NII, but widening HY spreads and elevated uncertainty cloud credit quality outlook.
Defensive staples positioning and largely domestic revenue base offer relative shelter from export-control and tariff escalation.
Global capex cycle is vulnerable to trade-war demand destruction signaled by falling oil and widening credit spreads.
